title: Periodontal health under different insulin therapies: a clinical study in patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus
summary:
People with type 1 diabetes develop periodontitis more often and at a younger age. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammation of the tissues supporting the teeth and can lead to tooth loss. Type 1 diabetes is treated either with an insulin pump or with several daily insulin injections. Whether the type of insulin therapy affects oral health has received little study so far.

This study examines 66 adults in three groups: people with type 1 diabetes using an insulin pump, people with type 1 diabetes using insulin injections, and people without diabetes. Participation consists of a single appointment of about 60 minutes in Munich or Rostock. At this appointment, teeth and gums are examined thoroughly and the amount of saliva is measured. In addition, samples of saliva, gum fluid, tongue coating and dental plaque are collected, as well as up to 30 ml of blood from an arm vein.

The samples are analysed for oral bacteria, inflammatory markers, and the genetic material and proteins of the participants. The results are intended to improve understanding of the relationship between blood glucose control, type of therapy and oral health. The aim is to identify markers that allow more targeted prevention and treatment of gum disease in type 1 diabetes. Participants receive a thorough dental examination and advice on their oral health.

interventions.name: Patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus on CSII therapy (continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion, insulin pump therapy). Single dental and periodontal examination (PD, CAL, BOP at 6 sites per tooth, tooth mobility, furcation involvement, DMFT, approximal plaque index with digital intraoral scan) and
Patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus on ICT therapy (intensified conventional insulin therapy with insulin injections). Examinations and sampling as in Arm 1.
Control group without diabetes, with confirmed normoglycaemia (HbA1c < 5.7 %). Examinations and sampling as in Arm 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ASA status 1 or 2
Written informed consent
Group 1: type 1 diabetes mellitus on CSII therapy (continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion)
Group 2: type 1 diabetes mellitus on ICT therapy (intensified conventional insulin therapy)
Group 3: no diabetes, confirmed normoglycaemia (HbA1c < 5.7 %)
Exclusion criteria:
ASA status ≥ 3
Inability to give informed consent
Acute inflammatory diseases outside the oral cavity
Fewer than 10 teeth
Pregnancy
Immunosuppression
